delegations.answer:
PARTIAL ANSWER: The adversary HyunKi Kim (hyunki1984@naver.com) sent a bragging email to Grace Hoppy with subject "All your datas belong to us" containing a pastebin link (https://pastebin.com/sdBUkwsE) and an attached screenshot (1534778082419.png). Grace Hoppy forwarded it to colleagues asking "Are these our customers?" The attacker also created a SOX transport rule (via compromised account fyodor@froth.ly) that BCCs hyunki1984@naver.com on all emails, and a SOX mailbox search for "cromdale OR beer OR financial OR secret" across all mailboxes. However, I was unable to retrieve the exact number of customer emails exposed — the count likely resides in the pastebin content, the screenshot attachment, or DLP alert sourcetypes (e.g., code42:security, symantec:ep:*) which I did not have enough tool calls to investigate.

UNCERTAINTY: I could not confirm the exact number of Frothly customer emails exposed. The pastebin URL content was not captured in stream:http, and I did not get to search DLP-related sourcetypes (code42:security, symantec:ep:risk:file, symantec:ep:security:file) or inspect the screenshot attachment for the count. "Taedonggang" was not found in any sourcetype I searched (o365:management:activity, stream:smtp, stream:http, ms:o365:management).
